items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: Buddy is my man. My right hand man. Ain't gonna find a better guy than Buddy Tate anywhere you go.

ctx.x: '67. I was working the Cafe Animal and my boss gave me the Sunday (phonetic) and I went to Austin, and it was on the set with Joe Jones, on drums, Illinois Jackson, me and Buddy Tate -- three Texas tenors.

And I put my best foot forward. You know why? Because of the thing we talked about prior to New York before I moved back to Texas and it never materialized -- I said, "I'm gonna show you how this thing could really go." That was what I was saying to myself, now. And ... I can lay down and be lazy, I could get up and play -- but you know, there ain't nobody that great. So you got to let people know.

items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: Buddy Tate is one of the oldest surviving alumni of the Count Basie Orchestra... known as one of the great “Texas Tenors” with Illinois Jacquet and Arnett Cobb.

ctx.x: Tenor saxophonist Buddy Tate is one of the oldest surviving alumni of the Count Basie Orchestra. Born George Holmes Tate on February 22, 1915, he grew up in Texas and later came to be known as one of the great “Texas Tenors” with Illinois Jacquet and Arnett Cobb. Buddy filled Herschel Evans’ chair in the Basie band and stayed from 1939-49. After Basie, a gig at the Celebrity Room in New York led to a stay of twenty years. He can be heard on records with Basie, Jimmy Rushing, Jay McShann and with numerous groups…

Buddy Tate was interviewed on March 3, 1995 in Scottsdale Arizona by Michael Woods. His daughter Georgette joined in part of the interview. Monk Rowe and Milt Fillius were also present during the interview.
